mainTopic: Are סימנים (identifying marks) a Torah-level way to prove ownership (דאורייתא), or only a rabbinic one (דרבנן)? The גמרא gives the practical difference and then tests several proofs.
overview: Just before this amud, the גמרא asked whether returning a lost item by its סימנים is דאורייתא or דרבנן. The amud opens with the practical difference: a lost גט can be returned by its marks only if סימנים are דאורייתא. The גמרא then brings three proofs that סימנים are דאורייתא: the שמלה teaching, the donkey's saddle, and the פסוק 'עד דרש אחיך אתו'. Each proof is pushed aside. Next, a משנה about identifying a dead man seems to show that סימנים are not דאורייתא. That proof is answered too, which leads to a discussion of which items people lend and which they never lend, such as saddles, pouches, purses and signet rings. The גמרא then tries to tie the question to a dispute between תנאים about a mole. Three different explanations show that the dispute does not have to depend on it. Finally, רבא explains why lost items are returned by סימנים even if they are only דרבנן. After רב ספרא's challenge, the reason given is that the owner himself agrees, and a case about found loan documents is shown to rest on simple logic instead.

steps.title: The practical difference: returning a lost גט by its marks
steps.stepSummary: The question of סימנים matters for a lost גט. If סימנים are דאורייתא, we return it. If they are only דרבנן, we do not, because רבנן can make rules about money but not about איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is whether we return a woman's גט based on identifying marks. If you say marks are from the Torah, we return it. If you say marks are rabbinic, then we cannot rely on them here. The רבנן made such an enactment for money matters, but they did not make one for matters of איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question 'what difference does it make?' by giving a case where the answer changes the הלכה: a lost גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, רבנן have the power to move ownership, so even a rabbinic סימן can be enough to give an item back. A גט, though, decides whether a woman is still an אשת איש, which is a Torah איסור. Rabbinic סימנים cannot carry that weight. So only if סימנים are דאורייתא can we hand the גט back to be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying marks used to prove an item is yours
Matters of what is forbidden or permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the stakes for the whole סוגיא. Each proof that follows is trying to settle whether a lost גט can be returned by its marks.

phrases.english: For returning a woman's bill of divorce based on identifying marks.
If you say they are from the Torah, we return it,
and if you say they are rabbinic,
when the Rabbis made an enactment, it was in money matters,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּאִיסּוּרָא – לָא עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא.
phrases.english: but in matters of prohibition, the Rabbis did not make an enactment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question 'למאי נפקא מינה' about whether סימנים are דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between saying סימנים are דאורייתא and saying they are דרבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A lost גט: it is returned by its סימנים only if they are דאורייתא, because רבנן do not make enactments in matters of איסור.

steps.title: Proof from the garment teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that compares all lost items to a שמלה, which 'has סימנים and has claimants.' Since סימנים are part of a Torah derivation, it seems they are דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The garment was already included in 'all of these.' So why was it mentioned on its own? To compare other things to it and to teach you this. A garment is special because it has marks and it has people who claim it, so the finder must announce it. In the same way, anything that has marks and has claimants must be announced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that סימנים are דאורייתא from the משנה that learns from the פסוק about a שמלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה learns from the Torah's mention of a שמלה that an item must be announced if it 'has סימנים.' If the Torah-level rule depends on סימנים, then סימנים must be a Torah-level way to identify an owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which opens a proof
To compare one thing to another
People who claim the item as theirs

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף הַשִּׂמְלָה הָיְתָה בִּכְלַל כׇּל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: Come and hear: The garment too was included in all of these,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:3 already says to return 'every lost thing of your brother,' and that includes a garment.

phrases.english: and why was it singled out? To compare to it,
and to tell you:
Just as a garment is special

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ סִימָנִין וְיֵשׁ לָהּ תּוֹבְעִין
phrases.english: in that it has marks and it has claimants,
and one is obligated to announce it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סִימָנִין
phrases.english: so too anything that has marks
and has claimants, one is obligated to announce it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף הַשִּׂמְלָה הָיְתָה בִּכְלַל כׇּל אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts trying to settle the question whose practical difference was just given.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה learning from שמלה that items 'with סימנים and claimants' must be announced.

steps.title: Only 'claimants' was really needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof aside. The משנה only needed the point about claimants, and it mentioned סימנים just in passing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא needed to teach about claimants. He mentioned marks just because they came along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the שמלה teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real Torah lesson is about תובעין, meaning an item whose owner is still looking for it. The word סימנים was added without being an essential part of the lesson, so it does not prove that סימנים are a Torah-level proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He mentioned it for no special reason

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying סימנים don't matter at all. It is only saying this משנה cannot prove they are דאורייתא.

phrases.english: The teacher needed 'claimants,'
'marks' he just mentioned along the way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the שמלה teaching; the main question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word סימנים in the משנה is not essential; the key point is תובעין.

steps.title: Proof from the donkey's saddle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching that a donkey is returned based on the סימנים of its saddle. That sounds like a Torah-level use of סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A donkey is returned by the marks of its saddle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof that סימנים are דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching is learned from the word 'חמור' in the Torah. If the Torah teaches that a donkey goes back to its owner because of saddle marks, then סימנים would seem to be דאורייתא.

phrases.english: Come and hear: A donkey, by the marks of the saddle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof fell, the גמרא tries a new one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that a donkey is returned by סימני אוכף.

steps.title: Read it as 'witnesses about the saddle'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording to 'witnesses of the saddle,' so the donkey is returned because of עדים, not סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: by witnesses about the saddle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the donkey proof by reading the teaching differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner has witnesses that the saddle is his, that is a full proof without any need for סימנים. So the teaching tells us nothing about whether סימנים are דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, which changes the wording

phrases.english: Say: 'by witnesses of the saddle.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing one word, so read it as witnesses testifying the saddle belongs to the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching can be read as relying on witnesses, not on סימנים.

steps.title: Proof from 'until your brother seeks it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק and reads 'דרש' as an order to check out the claimant to see if he is a cheat. This proof is set up here and finished next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And it shall be with you until your brother seeks it.' Could you think he would give it to him before the owner asks for it? Rather, it means: check him out, whether he is a cheat or not a cheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a third proof from a פסוק. It is setting up the next move, where it will ask how the finder checks the claimant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Obviously no one returns an item before its owner asks for it, so 'עד דרש' must mean something else: the finder must investigate the claimant. If this checking is done with סימנים, then the Torah itself relies on סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind?, which rules out the simple reading

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״וְהָיָה עִמְּךָ עַד דְּרֹשׁ אָחִיךָ אֹתוֹ״.
phrases.english: Come and hear: 'And it shall be with you until your brother seeks it.'
Could it enter your mind
that he would give it to him before he asks for it?!
Rather, investigate him, whether he is a cheat
or is not a cheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְהָיָה עִמְּךָ עַד דְּרֹשׁ אָחִיךָ אֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the donkey proof fell, the גמרא tries a third proof, this time straight from a פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reading of 'עד דרש אחיך אתו' as 'investigate whether the claimant is a cheat.'

steps.title: Checking the claimant must mean through identifying marks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the proof from step 6. Checking whether the claimant is a cheat must mean asking him for סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean we check him through identifying marks?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof it set up in step 6. 'Check out the claimant' must mean 'ask him for סימנים.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק itself tells us to check the claimant, and the way we check is through סימנים, then סימנים are part of a Torah command. That would make them דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean...? (opens a suggested proof)

phrases.english: What, is it not with identifying marks?
phrases.notes: This is about checking the claimant from step 6: isn't that done by asking him for marks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 6.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק's word 'דרש', read as a command to check the claimant

steps.title: No, the claimant is checked through witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The checking is done through עדים, not סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means through witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof from step 7. The claimant is checked by bringing עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does say to check the claimant, but it never says how. If the check is done with עדים, the פסוק tells us nothing about סימנים, so the proof falls away.

phrases.english: No, with witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The check could be done with עדים, so the פסוק does not prove anything about סימנים.
steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs that סימנים are דאורייתא (the שמלה, the saddle, and 'דרש') have been pushed aside.

steps.title: A משנה about identifying a dead man suggests marks are not Torah-level
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: you may only testify that a man died if you saw his face with the nose, even if there are marks on his body and clothes. So סימנים seem not to be דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: We only testify about the face together with the nose, even though there are marks on his body and his clothes. Learn from this that סימנים are not דאורייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tries a proof in the opposite direction. A משנה says body and clothing marks are not good enough to identify a dead man, so it seems סימנים are not דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the proofs tried to show סימנים are דאורייתא. Here the משנה refuses to rely on marks and demands the face itself, which suggests סימנים are not strong enough to count at the Torah level.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (opens a proof from a source)
The face, the full facial appearance

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. The earlier proofs tried to show סימנים ARE דאורייתא, but this one tries to show they are NOT.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We do not testify except
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יבמות about testifying that a man died, so his wife may remarry.

phrases.english: about the face together with the nose,
even though there are identifying marks
on his body and on his clothes.
Learn from this: identifying marks are not Torah-level!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַל פַּרְצוּף הַפָּנִים עִם הַחוֹטֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs for דאורייתא fail, the גמרא brings a proof for the other side.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה requiring the face with the nose to identify a dead man

steps.title: Body marks are too general, and clothes may have been lent
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Body marks here means general things like tall or short, and clothing marks fail only because the clothes might have been lent to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: 'His body' means that he was tall or short. 'His clothes' means we worry they were lent out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof from the משנה. It gives a separate reason why each kind of mark does not work there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body marks fail because they are weak and general, not because סימנים as a category don't count. The clothing marks may be real marks, but the clothes might have been lent to the dead man, so they don't prove who he is. Neither reason shows that good סימנים are not דאורייתא.

phrases.english: They say:
His body: that he is tall or short.
His clothes: because we worry about lending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both parts of the משנה, body and clothes
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The marks in the משנה fail for special reasons (too general, possible lending), not because סימנים are weak in general.

steps.title: If we worry about lending, how can a donkey be returned by its saddle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lending worry. If borrowing is a concern, the saddle could also be borrowed, so how can we return a donkey by the marks on its saddle?
steps.simpleTranslation: If we worry about lending, how do we return a donkey based on the marks of its saddle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 10. Worrying about lending seems to clash with returning a donkey by its saddle marks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saddle's marks show who owns the saddle, not necessarily who owns the donkey. If we worry that clothes were lent, we should also worry that the saddle was lent, and then the saddle should not prove anything.

phrases.english: If we worry about lending,
a donkey, by the marks of its saddle,
how do we return it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי חָיְישִׁינַן לִשְׁאֵלָה, חֲמוֹר בְּסִימָנֵי אוּכָּף הֵיכִי מַהְדְּרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lending concern raised in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The worry about lending used to explain the clothing marks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A saddle could be borrowed just like clothes, yet a donkey is returned by its saddle marks.

steps.title: People don't lend saddles because they hurt the donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people don't borrow saddles, because a saddle that isn't made for that donkey rubs it raw. So the saddle really points to the donkey's owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: a saddle is different. People don't borrow saddles, because a saddle hurts the donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11 by showing that saddles are not like clothes. People simply don't borrow them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothes get lent all the time, but a saddle is fitted to one donkey and wounds a different one. So there is no real worry that the saddle was borrowed, and its marks can show who owns the donkey.
steps.whatToRemember: The lending worry applies to things people actually lend, like clothes. Saddles aren't lent, so a saddle's marks can still identify the donkey's owner.

phrases.english: They say:
A saddle: people don't borrow a saddle,
because it wounds the donkey.
phrases.notes: A saddle made for one donkey doesn't fit another one well, so it rubs it raw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אוּכָּף, לָא שָׁאיְלִי אִינָשֵׁי אוּכָּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: saddles are not lent the way clothes are.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A saddle could be borrowed just like clothes, so its marks would prove nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: People don't lend saddles because they hurt the donkey, so the lending worry doesn't apply.

steps.title: Another answer: the clothing marks were only colors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second way to reject the proof from the משנה. The clothing 'marks' there were just general colors like white or red.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you prefer, say this instead: the marks on his clothes were only things like 'white' or 'red'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to push off the proof from the משנה about identifying a dead man. Clothing marks don't help there because they were only general colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, clothing marks failed because the clothes might have been lent out. Now the גמרא says the problem may be simpler: the marks were weak, like 'white' or 'red', which many garments share. So the משנה says nothing about whether real, specific סימנים work by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces another possible answer

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not replace the lending answer from step 10. It is a second option, and the next steps keep discussing the lending worry.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
His garments: where the marks were white or red.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second rejection of the proof from step 9, next to the lending explanation from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה about identifying a dead man.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The clothing marks in the משנה were vague colors, not real identifying marks, so the משנה tells us nothing about real סימנים.

steps.title: A ברייתא challenges the lending worry: a גט found tied to a pouch
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a lost גט found tied to a pouch, purse, or ring is valid. If we worry about lending, why isn't the pouch possibly someone else's?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if he found the גט tied to a pouch, a purse, or a ring, or among his clothes, even after a long time, it is valid. If we worry about lending, why is it valid when found tied to a pouch? Let us worry that the pouch was lent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the lending worry from step 10 using a ברייתא. In that ברייתא we trust a pouch to identify a lost גט and ignore the chance it was lent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a messenger who lost a גט rely on the pouch, purse, or ring it was tied to. If items are often lent, the pouch might belong to someone else, and the גט tied to it might be a different one. Since the ברייתא is not worried, it seems we don't worry about lending, and that weakens the answer from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: A signet ring, used to stamp a seal
We worry that it was lent

phrases.english: But that which is taught in a ברייתא:
If he found it tied to a pouch
phrases.notes: 'It' is a גט that the messenger lost. He is now trying to identify it.

phrases.english: or to a purse, or to a ring,
or if he found it among his garments,
even after a long time, it is valid.
And if you think that we worry about lending,
when he found it tied to a pouch,
why is it valid?
Let us worry about lending!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the saddle question was answered, this is a second challenge to the lending worry.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 10 that we worry clothing or items might have been lent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא trusts a pouch, purse, or ring to identify a lost גט. If lending were a real worry, it could not do that.

steps.title: People don't lend pouches, purses, or signet rings
steps.stepSummary: People don't lend out a pouch or purse because it is a bad sign for their luck. They don't lend a signet ring because someone could use it to forge documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: people do not lend a pouch, a purse, or a ring. A pouch and purse, because lending them is a bad sign. A ring, because someone could forge with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. These specific items are simply not lent, so the lending worry does not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the saddle in step 12, these are things people keep to themselves. A pouch or purse is not lent because people see it as a bad sign. A signet ring is not lent because a borrower could stamp false documents with it. So the lending worry still stands for clothing, but not for these items.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a sign (a bad omen)

steps.whatToRemember: The lending worry applies to things people normally lend, like clothes. It does not apply to things people never lend: a saddle, a pouch, a purse, or a signet ring.

phrases.english: They say:
A pouch, a purse, and a ring
people do not lend.
A pouch and a purse, because it is a bad sign;
and a ring, because one could forge with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: these items are never lent in real life.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's trust in a pouch seemed to show we don't worry about lending at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do worry about lending in general. Pouches, purses, and signet rings are an exception because people don't lend them.

steps.title: Maybe this is a dispute of תנאים about identifying by a mole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the question of סימנים being דאורייתא or דרבנן is the same as a dispute between the תנא קמא and אלעזר בן מהבאי about testifying on the basis of a mole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute of תנאים: One may not testify that a man died based on a mole. אלעזר בן מהבאי says: One may testify based on a mole. Isn't this what they argue about? The תנא קמא holds that סימנים are דרבנן, and אלעזר בן מהבאי holds that סימנים are דאורייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new approach. It suggests that our question is already argued about by תנאים in a ברייתא about identifying a dead man by a mole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting a woman remarry is a Torah-level matter. If a mole, which is a סימן, can't be used for it, that suggests סימנים are only דרבנן. If it can be used, סימנים are דאורייתא. The גמרא proposes that this is exactly the split between the two opinions. The words 'מאי לאו' show it is only a suggestion that the גמרא may still push back on.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is a dispute of תנאים
A mole or birthmark on the body
Is it not...? Introduces a suggested reading
By rabbinic law / by Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' and 'מאי לאו' mean the גמרא is only suggesting this reading. Don't treat it as the final answer yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the dispute really depends on this, then our question is simply an open argument between תנאים and is not settled by one clear source.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of the תנאים:
One does not testify based on a mole,
And Elazar ben Mahavai says:
One does testify based on a mole.
Is it not about this that they disagree?
That the first תנא holds:
identifying marks work only by rabbinic law,
and Elazar ben Mahavai holds:
identifying marks work by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the lending discussion and suggests the main question is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether סימנים are דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the תנא קמא and אלעזר בן מהבאי argue about testifying that a man died based on a mole.

steps.title: Maybe they argue about whether people born together share a mole
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone may agree that סימנים are דאורייתא. The argument is really about whether a mole is commonly found on a בן גילו, a person born at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that סימנים are from the Torah. Here they argue about whether a mole is often found on someone born at the same time. One opinion holds that it often is. The other holds that it usually is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the suggestion from step 16 that this argument is about whether סימנים are דאורייתא. He offers a different reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא's reading, both sides agree that a good סימן works on a Torah level. The question is whether a mole counts as a good סימן at all. If many people born at the same time share the same mole, it cannot point to one specific person.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying marks are valid proof on a Torah level
A mole or birthmark on the body
Someone born at the same time as him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סִימָנִין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: Everyone agrees that identifying marks are from the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּשׁוּמָא מְצוּיָה בְּבֶן גִּילוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether a mole is often found on one's contemporary.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: שׁוּמָא מְצוּיָה בְּבֶן גִּילוֹ,
phrases.english: One master holds: a mole is often found on one's contemporary,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, so he won't rely on a mole.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: שׁוּמָא אֵינָהּ מְצוּיָה בְּבֶן גִּילוֹ.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: a mole is not often found on one's contemporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: דכולי עלמא סימנין דאורייתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link that step 16 proposed between the mole argument and the question of whether סימנים are דאורייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the mole argument proves anything about whether סימנים are דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained as a factual question about how common moles are, even if everyone holds סימנים are דאורייתא.

steps.title: Maybe they argue about whether marks change after death
steps.stepSummary: A second way to push away the proof: everyone agrees a mole is not common among people born together. The argument is about whether body marks change after a person dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: Everyone agrees that a mole is not often found on someone born at the same time. Here they argue about whether marks tend to change after death. One opinion holds that they do change. The other holds that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another reason the two תנאים could be arguing, again without touching the question of סימנים being דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sides agree that a mole would be a fine סימן on a living person. The worry is that a body can look different after death. If so, the mole seen on the body may not be the same mark the man had in life. The תנא קמא is worried about this, and אלעזר בן מהבאי is not.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say instead (introduces another possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say: everyone agrees
that a mole is not often found on one's contemporary,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּסִימָנִין הָעֲשׂוּיִן לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether marks are likely to change after death.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: סִימָנִין עֲשׂוּיִם לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: One master holds: marks are likely to change after death.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: סִימָנִין אֵין עֲשׂוּיִם לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: marks are not likely to change after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא: דכולי עלמא שומא אינה מצויה בבן גילו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different explanation of the argument. It also rejects the proof from step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the same proof from step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument may be about whether a body changes after death, not about how strong סימנים are in Torah law.

steps.title: Maybe they argue about whether a mole is a very clear mark
steps.stepSummary: A third way: everyone agrees moles don't change after death, and everyone agrees ordinary סימנים are only דרבנן. The argument is whether a mole is a סימן מובהק, a very clear mark that works even on a Torah level.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: Everyone agrees that a mole does not change after death, and that סימנים are only from the Rabbis. Here they argue about whether a mole is a very clear mark. One opinion holds that a mole is a very clear mark. The other holds that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third reason for the argument. This time it says both sides even agree that regular סימנים are only דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if ordinary סימנים are only דרבנן, everyone agrees that a סימן מובהק (a very clear, specific mark) can be trusted for Torah matters. So the argument is only about which group a mole belongs to. אלעזר בן מהבאי says it is a סימן מובהק, and the תנא קמא says it is an ordinary סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying marks are only accepted by Rabbinic law
A very clear, specific identifying mark

steps.confusionAlert: The order of the opinions flips here. In this step, the first מר (the one who says a mole IS a very clear mark) is אלעזר בן מהבאי, not the תנא קמא.
steps.whatToRemember: The three answers all show the same thing: the mole argument can be explained without deciding whether סימנים are דאורייתא or דרבנן. So it does not settle that question.

phrases.english: If you want, say: everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּמָא אֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה,
phrases.english: that a mole is not likely to change after death,
and that identifying marks are from the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּשׁוּמָא סִימָן מוּבְהָק הוּא קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether a mole is a very clear mark.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: שׁוּמָא סִימָן מוּבְהָק הוּא,
phrases.english: One master holds: a mole is a very clear mark,
phrases.notes: This time the first opinion is אלעזר בן מהבאי, who does rely on a mole.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: שׁוּמָא לָאו סִימָן מוּבְהָק הוּא.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: a mole is not a very clear mark.

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא: דכולי עלמא שומא אינה עשויה להשתנות לאחר מיתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third explanation. This one assumes everyone holds סימנים are דרבנן, which closes the attempt in step 16 to tie the two questions together.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from step 16 even from the side of those who hold סימנים are דרבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone can agree about the strength of ordinary סימנים and still argue about whether a mole is a סימן מובהק.

steps.title: How can lost items be returned by marks if marks are only Rabbinic?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks a question: if סימנים are not דאורייתא, how are we allowed to give back a lost item based on them?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If you say that identifying marks are not from the Torah, how do we return a lost item based on marks?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a problem for the view that סימנים are only דרבנן. He answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סימנים are not real Torah proof, then the person describing the item has not truly proven it is his. In that case, giving him the item might mean taking it from its real owner. So how can the הלכה tell the finder to return it based on סימנים?

keyTerms.meaning: If you end up saying (if we take that position)

phrases.english: Rava said: If you say
that identifying marks are not from the Torah,
how do we return a lost item based on marks?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: אם תמצי לומר סימנין לאו דאורייתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the view that סימנים are דרבנן is still possible, רבא now asks how the הלכה of returning lost items works under that view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that סימנים are only דרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without Torah-level proof, returning the item based on סימנים could hand someone else's property to the wrong person.

steps.title: The finder is glad to return items by marks
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the finder is happy to return lost items based on סימנים. That way, if he ever loses something, others will return it to him based on סימנים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the finder of a lost item is happy to return it based on marks. That way, when he loses something himself, people will also return it to him based on marks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The return does not rest on Torah-level proof. It rests on what the finder wants. Every finder knows he could lose something someday, so he agrees to a system where items are returned based on סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is pleasing to him, he is happy with it
The finder of a lost item

phrases.english: Because it is pleasing to the finder of a lost item
to return it based on marks,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּכִי אָבְדָה לֵיהּ לְדִידֵהּ
phrases.english: so that when something is lost from him himself,
they will also return it to him based on marks.

steps.triggerLanguage: דניחא ליה למוצא אבידה דנהדר בסימנין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different basis for the halacha: the finder's own consent and interest, not Torah-level proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Returning by סימנים seemed to need Torah-level proof, which דרבנן סימנים do not give.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder agrees to return by סימנים for his own future benefit, so the return is justified.

steps.title: The finder cannot give away someone else's property
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges רבא: how can the finder make a deal for his own benefit using an item that belongs to someone else?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to רבא: Can a person do a favor for himself with money that is not his?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks the answer רבא just gave in Step 21. A finder has no right to risk the real owner's item just so that people will return his own things one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason depended on the finder agreeing to return items by סימנים. But the lost item is not the finder's. If a liar describes it and takes it, the real owner loses, not the finder. So the finder's agreement means nothing here.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with רבא here
Money or property that is not his

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Rava:
But does a person do a favor for himself
with money that is not his?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה טוֹבָה לְעַצְמוֹ בְּמָמוֹן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the finder's agreement allows returning items by סימנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The finder cannot agree on behalf of the owner, because the item is not his.

steps.title: The owner himself wants items returned by clear marks
steps.stepSummary: The new reason: the owner of the lost item agrees to the סימנים system, because he believes only he knows the clear marks of his own item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the owner of the lost item is happy to be able to give marks and take it back. He knows he has no witnesses, and he says: nobody else knows its clear marks, and I will give its clear marks and take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the agreement from the finder to the owner. The owner is happy with the סימנים system, because without it he could never get his item back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes רב ספרא's problem, since now the person who agrees is the person who owns the item. The owner usually has no witnesses, so סימנים are his only hope. He trusts that a stranger would not know the clear marks, so he does not fear that someone else will take it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is good for him, he is happy with it
The owner of the lost item

steps.whatToRemember: We return lost items by סימנים because the owner himself agrees to it. He has no witnesses, and he trusts that only he knows the clear marks.

phrases.english: Rather, the owner of the lost item is happy
to give marks and take it.
He knows well that he has no witnesses,
and he says:
Nobody else knows
its clear marks,
and I will give its clear marks
and take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to Step 20 after Step 22 knocked down the old one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source of agreement: the owner agrees, not the finder
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The finder's agreement allows returning items by סימנים
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner's own agreement allows it, because he trusts that only he knows the clear marks

steps.title: The case of found loan documents seems to go against the owner
steps.stepSummary: The question uses רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling about found loan documents. Returning them to the lender cannot be something the borrower is happy with.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the משנה where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if one person borrowed from three, return the documents to the borrower. If three borrowed from one, return them to the lender. Is the borrower happy to have them returned to the lender?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new 'owner agrees' reason with a case where the item goes to someone the other side would never agree to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If items are returned only because the people involved agree, then the borrower would never agree to give his loan documents to the lender. The lender could then use them to collect from him. So something other than agreement must be at work.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא quoted in the משנה

phrases.english: But what about that which we learned:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who borrowed from three – return them to the borrower,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁלָּווּ מִן הָאֶחָד – יַחְזִיר לַמַּלְוֶה.
phrases.english: three who borrowed from one – return them to the lender.

phrases.aramaic: נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְלֹוֶה לְאַהְדּוֹרֵי לֵיהּ לְמַלְוֶה?
phrases.english: Is the borrower happy to have it returned to the lender?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'owner agrees' reason from Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that returning lost items depends on the agreement of the people involved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the loan documents case the item goes to the lender, even though the borrower would never agree to that.

steps.title: The loan documents ruling is based on simple logic
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the loan documents case is not about agreement or סימנים. It is about logic: we figure out who most likely dropped the documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is simple logic. If one borrowed from three, return to the borrower, because such documents are usually found with the borrower and not with a lender, so they must have fallen from the borrower. If three borrowed from one, return to the lender, because such documents are usually found with the lender and not with a borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling works differently. We are not relying on anyone agreeing. We are working out who the real owner is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bundle of documents usually stays with the one person they all have in common. When one borrower owes three lenders, that common person is the borrower. When three borrowers owe one lender, it is the lender. So the documents go to whoever logically dropped them, and the 'owner agrees' reason is not challenged.
steps.whatToRemember: Returning items by סימנים rests on the owner's agreement. The found loan documents case is decided by logic about who most likely dropped them.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, it is logic,
phrases.notes: רבא is answering. The documents go back because of reasoning, not because of סימנים or anyone agreeing.

phrases.english: one who borrowed from three, return them to the borrower,
because they are commonly found with the borrower,
they are not commonly found with a lender.
Conclude from this that they fell from the borrower.
Three who borrowed from one, return them to the lender,
because they are commonly found with the lender,
they are not commonly found with a borrower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: that ruling is based on logic about ownership, not on agreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loan documents ruling also depends on the parties agreeing, so it would fail
steps.terutzMaskana: The documents go to whoever logically dropped them, so the 'owner agrees' reason still stands
